title: Spent a year building a D&D tabletop with an AI DM. The hardest part was getting it to shut up
author: TallBoyPirateSqaud
selftext:
I've been building this for about a year. It's a virtual tabletop for D&D 5e that runs itself: maps, combat, dice, character sheets, and an AI DM running the story.



The first thing I learned is that the AI can't be in charge of the rules. When it was, it handed out magic swords and forgot who had the key. So the game owns everything that's real (HP, gold, items, where everyone is standing) and the DM can only give you what the game can actually track. If it says the door is locked, it's locked on the board.



Lately the hardest part has been getting the DM to talk less lol. I'd type five words and get 150 back. Hard capping it made the dialogue choppy and weird, so now I'm working on it saying less instead of getting cut off.



Favorite moment from my last playtest: I carried a dead miller home from the woods so the village sin-eater could eat the bread off his chest. He does it, and a voice that isn't his comes out of him asking "Is anyone weeping yet?" Pretty sure I said "nope" out loud.



Built mostly with Claude Code. There's a written campaign underneath so it isn't just random quests.



Still early and not open yet, I'm getting a small group together to playtest first. If you want to follow along or help test:
